findings.element: h2.b-measureHead ("DAYS AWAY") against h1.b-who ("MARA & FINN") on state=print, [data-medium="sheet"]
findings.problem: On the printed A4 keepsake the two heads that name the spread do not sit on one line. Driven at 794x1123 under emulateMedia("print"), in ?v=paper and ?v=ink alike (print forces the paper ground, so this is identical in both rooms): .b-two opens both tracks at y=41 with grid-template-columns computing to "220px 420px"; h1.b-who sets its ink at y=41 and h2.b-measureHead at y=61, because the head keeps margin-top: 20px. On every screen state that stands the same two columns side by side the two heads share a line exactly - both at y=108.39 at 1440, 1280 and 1152, owner-flight and desk. The cause is b.css:1378, `[data-medium="full"] .b-two > * > *:first-child > .b-measureHead { margin-top: 0 }`, whose own comment states the intent verbatim: the 20px "is taken back only where the columns actually stand side by side". The sheet DOES stand them side by side and is [data-medium="sheet"], so the selector never reaches it. Neither gate looks: "the sheet keeps its composition on paper" only counts grid tracks (=== 2), and "and the heads are one object" only compares type specs, never position. This is the one output that cannot be reflowed after it exists - it is handed to the venue and the celebrant on the morning.
findings.fix: Add the sheet medium to the same selector in b.css:1378, inside the existing @media (min-width: 701px) block: `[data-medium="full"] .b-two > * > *:first-child > .b-measureHead, [data-medium="sheet"] .b-two > * > *:first-child > .b-measureHead { margin-top: 0; }`. Injected and re-measured at 794x1123 under print media: both heads land on y=41 and .b-print stays 1119.31px tall against a 1123px page, so the keepsake is still one sheet.

findings.problem: The head's left edge is not set by a decision - it is wherever the string happens to land, because the head is text-align:right inside a fixed box (76px, widened to 84px at >=701 by b.css:1372). Measured ink-left in both rooms: at 390-700 the 75.3px string nearly fills the 76px box, so the head reads flush (+0.75 off the margin). From 701 to 1023 the box is 84px and the head sits at 104.75 while .b-who, .b-todayLabel, .b-gapNote and .b-behindLabel all stand on 96 - it is the only element on that screen off the page margin, and it is plainly visible in the 768x1024 frame this panel was given. At >=1024 the same 8.75px separates the two section heads of the right-hand column from each other: .b-behindLabel ink-left 586 against .b-measureHead 594.75 at 1440 (496 against 504.75 at 1024 and 1152), on owner-flight and desk, paper and ink. The surface already shows the reader the flush version - on day and phone the box stays 76 and "DAYS BACK" sets flush with "BEHIND YOU" - so one product presents the same head both ways for no reason a reader can see.
findings.fix: Change `text-align: right` to `text-align: left` on .b-measureHead (b.css:144); keep width and white-space: nowrap as they are. Injected and measured: at 768 the head joins .b-who / .b-todayLabel / .b-gapNote / .b-behindLabel on 96; at 1440 it joins .b-behindLabel on 586 so the whole right column reads on one left edge. The .b-away day figures keep their own right-aligned lane and do not move (advance-box right edge stays 670 at 1440, 180 at 768).

findings.element: p.b-who x2 on state=publish - "What lands in the message" and "The link"
findings.problem: shell.css:123 and :56 declare --size-labelWide (12px) and --track-labelWide (0.20em) as "the ceremonial top line, and only that". Every section head in the product sets at --size-label / --track-label - 11px, 1.76px tracking, 0.62 ink: DAYS AWAY, BEHIND YOU, HAPPENING NOW, TODAY IS 16 JULY, THE DAY, SCAN FOR THE LIVE PLAN. The two heads that name publish's columns set at 12px with 2.4px tracking instead, measured identically in paper and ink. So the screen the owner lands on from "Get the link" heads its two columns with a different typographic object from the screen they just left, in the same position on the page, and the two spreads do not read as one grid. Publish's .b-who is already a hybrid rather than a decision: it carries the identity line's size and tracking with a section head's 0.62 alpha, while the identity .b-who on every other state is full ink.
findings.fix: Add `[data-state="publish"] .b-press .b-who { font-size: var(--size-label); letter-spacing: var(--track-label); }` to b.css. Verified by injection in both rooms: the two column heads move to 11px / 1.76px and p.b-ogWho inside the preview card is untouched at 12px / 2.4px, which is correct - there it really is the card's own top line.

biggestWin: The counter block is set the way a studio sets a display figure and nothing else on this surface contradicts it. The 148px "79" hangs 7.39px left of the 344px column so its optical edge, not its advance box, stands on the margin; "days" sits on the figure's exact baseline (both at 386.69 at 1440); and out in the measure the 17px gutter figure is cap-centred against the 24px title to within 0.4px (cap centres 563.2 and 563.6) rather than lazily baseline-matched. That care holds across the whole system: one 56px gutter and one 344px rail from 390 to 1920, the pane fade written only when there is content past the edge, the reversibility bar given a real 344px band in layout instead of floating over the count, the artifact card padded 40 top / 56 bottom and the ended card 100 / 110 so both sit optically rather than mathematically centred. The composition is at the benchmark; what I found is three places where two objects that should share an edge do not.
